items.name: Weierstrass preparation over Z_p[[T]]
items.statement: Every nonzero g ∈ Λ ≅ Z_p[[T]] is uniquely u·p^μ·Q(T) with u ∈ Λ^×, μ ∈ Z_{≥0} and Q a distinguished polynomial of degree λ; λ(g), μ(g) are the Iwasawa invariants of g.
items.note: Mathlib proves Weierstrass factorization in a power series ring over a complete local ring (PowerSeries.exists_isWeierstrassFactorization, with distinguished polynomials Polynomial.IsDistinguishedAt); extracting p^μ first is routine. Iwasawa invariants of modules are the next item.

items.name: Characteristic ideals and Iwasawa invariants of Λ-modules
items.statement: For a finitely generated torsion Λ-module X, char_Λ(X) is the product of the elementary divisors in the structure theorem up to pseudo-isomorphism; λ(X), μ(X) are the invariants of a generator. For nonzero L ∈ Λ^ur, λ(L), μ(L) are those of an element of Λ generating the same Λ^ur-ideal. A torsion X with μ = 0 and no nonzero finite submodule is Z_p-free of rank λ(X), so λ(X) = dim_{F_p} X/pX.
items.locator: Introduction §0.2, p. 4; §1.2, proof of Proposition 1.2.5, pp. 8–9
items.note: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L4 plans Weierstrass theory, the structure theorem up to pseudo-isomorphism and characteristic ideals.

items.name: Selmer groups and Tate–Shafarevich groups of elliptic curves
items.statement: For L ⊂ Q̄, Sel_{p^m}(E/L) sits in 0 → E(L) ⊗ Z/p^m → Sel_{p^m}(E/L) → Ш(E/L)[p^m] → 0, and Sel_{p^∞}(E/L) = lim→ Sel_{p^m}(E/L).
items.note: The Tau Ceti roadmap Elliptic curves plans Selmer groups and Sha (Layer 7).

items.name: The anticyclotomic main conjectures in BDP and Heegner-point form
items.statement: Let E/Q, p > 2 good ordinary, K imaginary quadratic with (Heeg) every ℓ | N split in K; Γ = Gal(K_∞/K) for the anticyclotomic Z_p-extension, Λ = Z_p[[Γ]], Λ_ac = Λ ⊗ Q_p, Λ^ur = Λ ⊗̂ Z_p^ur. Conjecture A (with (spl) p = v v̄ split): the dual 𝔛_E of the Selmer group of E over K_∞ relaxed at v and strict at v̄ is Λ-torsion and char_Λ(𝔛_E)Λ^ur = (L_E), L_E the BDP p-adic L-function. Conjecture B (with (disc): D_K odd, D_K ≠ −3): with 𝒮 = (lim_n lim_m Sel_{p^m}(E/K_n)) ⊗ Q_p, κ_1^Hg ∈ 𝒮 the Λ_ac-adic Heegner class, ℋ = Λ_ac κ_1^Hg and 𝒳 = Sel_{p^∞}(E/K_∞)^∨ ⊗ Q_p, both 𝒮 and 𝒳 have Λ_ac-rank one and char(𝒳_tors) = char(𝒮/ℋ)².
items.locator: Introduction §0.1, Conjectures A and B, pp. 1–2
items.note: HE.8b states the Heegner-point characteristic-ideal formula and its Greenberg/BDP version char(X_Gr)Λ^ur = (L_BDP²); ModularIwasawaMainConjectures L6 owns the formulation interfaces. The paper's L_E is already the square.

items.name: Iwasawa modules of characters and their local Euler factors
items.statement: For θ : G_K → F_p^× (Teichmüller-lifted to Z_p^×) with conductor divisible only by primes split in K, M_θ = Z_p(θ) ⊗ Λ^∨ with G_K acting by θ ⊗ Ψ^{−1}, Ψ : G_K → Γ ⊂ Λ^×. For w | ℓ ≠ p split in K, γ_w the image of Frob_w in Γ_w ⊂ Γ and P_w = det(1 − Frob_w X | Q_p(θ)_{I_w}), set 𝒫_w(θ) = P_w(ℓ^{−1}γ_w) ∈ Λ (1.1). Similarly M_E = T_pE ⊗ Λ^∨ and 𝒫_w(E) = P_w(ℓ^{−1}γ_w) with P_w = det(1 − Frob_w X | V_{I_w}).
items.note: The residual-character Iwasawa modules that BSD.7a asks for.

items.name: Local Iwasawa cohomology of M_θ and M_E
items.statement: (Lemma 1.1.1) For w ∤ p split in K, H¹(K_w, M_θ)^∨ is Λ-torsion with char = (𝒫_w(θ)), hence μ = 0; likewise for M_E with 𝒫_w(E). (Proposition 1.1.3) For w | p (p split) with θ|_{G_w} ≠ 1, ω: restriction H¹(K_w, M_θ) → H¹(I_w, M_θ)^{G_w/I_w} is an isomorphism, and H¹(K_w, M_θ) is Λ-cofree of rank 1. (Lemma 1.3.1) For w | p with E(K_w)[p] = 0, H¹(K_w, M_E) is Λ-cofree of rank 2.
items.locator: §1.1, Lemma 1.1.1, Proposition 1.1.3, pp. 6–7; §1.3, Lemma 1.3.1, p. 10; end of §1.4, p. 12
items.note: Lemma 1.1.1 adapts Greenberg–Vatsal Prop. 2.4 (w finitely decomposed in K_∞). The cofreeness uses Lemma 1.1.2, the sequence 0 → Q_p/Z_p(θ) → M_θ →T M_θ → 0 and the local Euler characteristic.

items.name: A freeness criterion over Λ
items.statement: If X is a finitely generated Λ-module with X[T] = 0 and X/TX free over Z_p of rank r, then X is Λ-free of rank r.
items.note: Nakayama twice and the snake lemma; a module-structure fact for PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L4.

items.name: Greenberg Selmer groups of characters and of E
items.statement: For Σ a finite set of places of K containing ∞, the primes above p and the conductor, all finite ones split in K, and S = Σ ∖ {v, v̄, ∞}: H¹_{F_Gr}(K, M) = ker(H¹(K^Σ/K, M) → ∏_{w∈Σ, w∤p} H¹(K_w, M) × H¹(K_v̄, M)) and the S-imprimitive H¹_{F_Gr^S}(K, M) = ker(H¹(K^Σ/K, M) → H¹(K_v̄, M)), for M = M_θ or M_E, and their residual versions with M[p]; 𝔛_θ, 𝔛_θ^S, 𝔛_E, 𝔛_E^S are the Pontryagin duals.
items.note: Relaxed at v, strict at v̄, strict away from p; independent of Σ.

items.name: Rubin's main conjecture for imaginary quadratic fields, anticyclotomic character components
items.statement: For θ as above with p ∤ |Δ_θ|, H¹(K^Σ/K_θ, M_θ) ≅ Hom((𝒳_∞^Σ)^θ, Q_p/Z_p), and with the unramified-outside-v Galois group 𝒳_∞ of K_∞K_θ, char_Λ((𝒳_∞)^θ) is generated by the anticyclotomic θ-projection of the Katz p-adic L-function (Rubin); in particular λ(𝔛_θ) = λ(L_θ) (used in Theorem 2.2.3).
items.locator: §1.2, proof of Theorem 1.2.2 and Remark 1.2.3, p. 8; §2.2, proof of Theorem 2.2.3, p. 16
items.note: Rubin, Invent. Math. 103 (1991). Needs the two-variable main conjecture and its anticyclotomic descent; D_K ≠ −3, −4 keeps p ∤ |O_K^×|.

items.name: Hida: μ = 0 for anticyclotomic Katz p-adic L-functions
items.statement: For an odd prime p and a p-ordinary CM field, the anticyclotomic Katz p-adic L-function with branch character whose conductor is a product of primes split over the maximal real subfield has μ = 0, except in the rare cases where the root number of its p-adic functional equation is ≡ −1 mod p.
items.locator: §1.2, proof of Theorem 1.2.2, p. 8; §2.2, proof of Theorem 2.2.2, p. 15
items.note: Hida, Ann. of Math. 172 (2010). The paper applies it to θ = φ, ψ restricted to G_K, whose conductors are divisible only by primes split in K.

items.name: Residual characters: Selmer modules are torsion with μ = 0 and computable λ
items.statement: Assume θ|_{G_v̄} ≠ 1, ω. (Theorem 1.2.2, Rubin–Hida) 𝔛_θ is Λ-torsion with μ = 0. (Lemma 1.2.4, needs only θ|_{G_v̄} ≠ 1) H¹_{F_Gr^S}(K, M_θ[p]) ≅ H¹_{F_Gr^S}(K, M_θ)[p]. (Proposition 1.2.5) 𝔛_θ^S is Λ-torsion with μ = 0, λ(𝔛_θ^S) = λ(𝔛_θ) + Σ_{w∈Σ, w∤p} λ(𝒫_w(θ)), and H¹_{F_Gr^S}(K, M_θ[p]) is finite of dimension λ(𝔛_θ^S). (Corollary 1.2.6) H²(K^Σ/K, M_θ[p]) = 0 and 0 → H¹_{F_Gr^S}(K, M_θ[p]) → H¹(K^Σ/K, M_θ[p]) → H¹(K_v̄, M_θ[p]) → 0 is exact.
items.note: Uses Pollack–Weston Prop. A.2 (surjectivity of the global-to-local map), H² = 0 via the Euler characteristic, no pseudo-null submodules (Greenberg, Prop. 5) and Greenberg–Vatsal Lemma 2.6. The proof of Proposition 1.2.5 cites a nonexistent Proposition 1.1.3(iii) (sourceIssues).

items.name: Residual comparison for E and the algebraic Iwasawa invariants
items.statement: Let E/Q have good reduction at p, a rational p-isogeny 0 → F_p(φ) → E[p] → F_p(ψ) → 0 with φψ = ω, every ℓ | N split in K and p split in K; assume φ|_{G_p} ≠ 1, ω. (Proposition 1.4.1) 0 → H¹_{F_Gr^S}(K, M_φ[p]) → H¹_{F_Gr^S}(K, M_E[p]) → H¹_{F_Gr^S}(K, M_ψ[p]) → 0 is exact, so dim H¹_{F_Gr^S}(K, M_E[p]) = λ(𝔛_φ^S) + λ(𝔛_ψ^S). (Proposition 1.4.2) H¹_{F_Gr^S}(K, M_E[p]) ≅ H¹_{F_Gr^S}(K, M_E)[p], and 𝔛_E^S, 𝔛_E are Λ-torsion with μ = 0. (Corollary 1.4.3) 𝔛_E^S has no nonzero finite submodule and λ(𝔛_E^S) = dim H¹_{F_Gr^S}(K, M_E[p]). (Theorem 1.5.1) 𝔛_E is Λ-torsion, μ(𝔛_E) = 0 and λ(𝔛_E) = λ(𝔛_φ) + λ(𝔛_ψ) + Σ_{w∈S}{λ(𝒫_w(φ)) + λ(𝒫_w(ψ)) − λ(𝒫_w(E))}.
items.note: The anticyclotomic analogue of Greenberg–Vatsal's cyclotomic comparison; this is the residual-character comparison BSD.7a plans.

items.name: The Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna p-adic L-function
items.statement: With 𝔑 ⊂ O_K, O_K/𝔑 ≅ Z/N, there is L_E ∈ Λ^ur such that for every character ξ of Γ crystalline at v and v̄ with Hecke infinity type (n, −n), n > 0, n ≡ 0 mod p − 1: L_E(ξ) = (Ω_p/Ω_∞)^{4n}·Γ(n)Γ(n+1)ξ(𝔑^{−1})/(4(2π)^{2n+1}√D_K^{2n−1})·(1 − a_pξ(v̄)p^{−1} + ξ(v̄)²p^{−1})²·L(f/K, ξ, 1). It is the square of the Castella–Hsieh measure 𝓛_{v,η}(η^{−1}ξ) built from the Serre–Tate expansions of the p-depletion f^♭ at CM points x_𝔞 on the Igusa tower.
items.note: GZ.9 constructs the BDP/Brooks p-adic L-function at a good prime split in K, with its interpolation range, CM periods, removed Euler factors and the square/square-root distinction.

items.name: Anticyclotomic projections of Katz p-adic L-functions
items.statement: For a Dirichlet character θ of conductor C | N (so p ∤ C) and 𝔆 | 𝔑 with O_K/𝔆 = Z/C, there is L_θ ∈ Λ^ur with, for ξ as in Theorem 2.1.1, L_θ(ξ) = (Ω_p/Ω_∞)^{2n}·4Γ(n+1)(2πi)^{n−1}/√D_K^{n−1}·(1 − θ^{−1}(p)ξ^{−1}(v))(1 − θ(p)ξ(v̄)p^{−1})·∏_{ℓ|C}(1 − θ(ℓ)ξ(w)ℓ^{−1})·L(θ_Kξ𝐍_K, 0); it is the image of Katz's measure (Kriz, Thm. 27) under π_θ : g ↦ θ(g)[g].
items.note: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3 constructs Katz's p-adic L-function for p-ordinary CM types; the projection along a branch character is a specialisation of that measure. The paper also uses L_ψ, whose conductor is divisible by p, which this statement does not cover (sourceIssues).

items.name: Kriz's congruence between the BDP and Katz p-adic L-functions
items.statement: Assume E[p]^ss ≅ F_p(φ) ⊕ F_p(ψ), labelled so that p ∤ cond(φ), and φ ≠ 1. Then N/N_0 = N_+N_- (N_0 the square-full part) with a_ℓ ≡ φ(ℓ) (ℓ | N_+), a_ℓ ≡ ψ(ℓ) (ℓ | N_-), a_ℓ ≡ 0 (ℓ | N_0) mod p, and L_E ≡ (𝓔^ι_{φ,ψ})²·(L_φ)² mod pΛ^ur, where 𝓔_{φ,ψ} = ∏_{ℓ|N_0N_-} 𝒫_w(φ)·∏_{ℓ|N_0N_+} 𝒫_w(ψ), w | ℓ the prime dividing 𝔑, and ι : γ ↦ γ^{−1}.
items.note: f ≡ G mod p for a weight-two Eisenstein series G (Kriz, Thm. 34, Rem. 32); Kriz's Prop. 37 gives L_G = 𝓔^ι_{φ,ψ}·L_φ (2.7), and the congruence of Serre–Tate expansions gives L_E ≡ L_G² mod p. The proof cites 'Theorem 2.2.1' for the interpolation property of L_φ, meaning Theorem 2.1.2 (sourceIssues).

items.name: Analytic Iwasawa invariants and their equality with the algebraic ones
items.statement: (Theorem 2.2.2) Under the hypotheses of Theorem 2.2.1, μ(L_E) = 0 and λ(L_E) = λ(L_φ) + λ(L_ψ) + Σ_{w∈S}{λ(𝒫_w(φ)) + λ(𝒫_w(ψ)) − λ(𝒫_w(E))}, using λ(L_ψ) = λ(L_φ) from the functional equation of the Katz p-adic L-function. (Theorem 2.2.3) If moreover φ|_{G_p} ≠ 1, ω, then μ(L_E) = μ(𝔛_E) = 0 and λ(L_E) = λ(𝔛_E).
items.note: Combines Theorem 2.2.1, Hida's μ = 0, Theorem 1.5.1 and Rubin's λ(L_θ) = λ(𝔛_θ). The Euler-factor bookkeeping (2.10) was checked prime by prime: for ℓ | N_+, 𝒫_w(E) ≡ 𝒫_w(φ); for ℓ | N_0, 𝒫_w(E) = 1; for ℓ ∤ N, 𝒫_w(E) ≡ 𝒫_w(φ)𝒫_w(ψ) mod p.

items.name: Selmer structures, transverse conditions and Kolyvagin systems
items.statement: For a complete Noetherian local (R, 𝔪) with finite residue field of characteristic p and an R[G_K]-module M unramified outside a finite set: a Selmer structure F is a finite set Σ(F) of places (containing ∞, the primes above p and the ramified ones) with local conditions H¹_F(K_w, M) ⊂ H¹(K_w, M), and H¹_F(K, M) is the kernel of H¹(K^Σ/K, M) → ∏_{w∈Σ} H¹(K_w, M)/H¹_F(K_w, M); H¹_f = H¹_ur at w ∤ p where M is unramified, H¹_s the singular quotient. 𝓛_0 is the set of primes ℓ ≠ p inert in K with M unramified at ℓ; H¹_tr(K_λ, T) = ker(H¹(K_λ, T) → H¹(K[ℓ]_{λ′}, T)); F^a_b(c) is relaxed at a, strict at b, transverse at c. I_ℓ is the smallest ideal containing ℓ + 1 with Frob_λ trivial on T/I_ℓT, and φ^fs_λ : H¹_f(K_λ, T/I_ℓT) ≃ T/I_ℓT ≃ H¹_s(K_λ, T/I_ℓT) ⊗ G_ℓ (3.1), G_ℓ = Gal(K[ℓ]/K[1]). A Kolyvagin system for (T, F, 𝓛) is {κ_n ∈ H¹_{F(n)}(K, T/I_nT) ⊗ G_n}_{n∈𝒩} with (φ^fs_λ ⊗ 1)(loc_λ κ_n) = loc_λ κ_{nℓ}.
items.note: SelmerIwasawaCohomology L2 plans Selmer structures; EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.1 the transverse condition and the finite–singular comparison; HeegnerPointEulerSystems HE.5 Howard's Heegner version with inert auxiliary primes. The definitions have misprints (sourceIssues).

items.name: Anticyclotomic twists of T_pE and the error constants
items.statement: For E/Q of conductor N, p ∤ 2N good ordinary, K with D_K prime to Np and (h1) E(K)[p] = 0, and α : Γ → R^× (R the integers of a finite Φ/Q_p, r = rank_{Z_p}R): T_α = T_pE ⊗ R(α), V_α, A_α = V_α/T_α; T̄ ≅ E[p] ⊗ R/𝔪 (3.2), so T̄^{G_K} = 0. F_ord is the ordinary structure (image of H¹(K_w, Fil⁺_w V_α) at w | p, unramified at w | N), propagated to T_α and A_α. The error constants are C_α = v_p(α(γ) − α^{−1}(γ)) for α ≠ α^{−1} and 0 otherwise (3.3); C_1 = min{v_p(u − 1) : u ∈ U}, where U = Z_p^× ∩ im(ρ_E|_{G_{K_∞}}) is open in Z_p^× and lies in im(ρ_α) for every α (Lemma 3.3.3); C_2 = min{m : p^m End(T_pE) ⊂ ρ_E(Z_p[G_Q])}, so that p^{C_2} kills End_R(T)/ρ(R[G_{K_∞}]) (Lemma 3.3.4). If ρ_E is surjective then C_1 = 0; if E[p] is irreducible then C_2 = 0 (Remark 3.3.5). 𝓛_E = {ℓ ∈ 𝓛_0(T_pE) : a_ℓ ≡ ℓ + 1 ≡ 0 mod p}.
items.note: ρ_E(G_{K_∞}) = ρ_E(G_Q) because K is ramified at a prime not dividing Np, so Q(E[p^∞]) ∩ K_∞ = Q. These constants replace the big-image hypothesis of Howard and Mazur–Rubin.

items.name: Structure of Selmer groups of the twists
items.statement: For n ∈ 𝒩^{(k)} (squarefree products of ℓ ∈ 𝓛 with I_ℓ ⊂ p^kR) and 0 ≤ i ≤ k: H¹_{F(n)}(K, T^{(k)}/𝔪^iT^{(k)}) ≅ H¹_{F(n)}(K, T^{(k)}[𝔪^i]) ≅ H¹_{F(n)}(K, T^{(k)})[𝔪^i] (Lemma 3.3.1); and H¹_{F(n)}(K, T^{(k)}) ≅ (R^{(k)})^ε ⊕ M^{(k)}(n) ⊕ M^{(k)}(n) with ε ∈ {0, 1} independent of k and n (Proposition 3.3.2).
items.note: Mazur–Rubin Lem. 3.5.4 (with the cartesian property, Lem. 3.7.1) and Howard Prop. 1.5.5 and the parity Lemma 1.5.3, which need only T̄^{G_K} = 0 and Howard's (H.3)–(H.4).

items.name: Čebotarev argument with error terms
items.statement: Suppose α ≠ 1 and let e = r(C_1 + C_2 + C_α). (Proposition 3.3.6) For c_1, c_2, c_3 ∈ H¹(K, T^{(k)}) with Rc_1 + Rc_2 containing 𝔪^{d_1}R^{(k)} ⊕ 𝔪^{d_2}R^{(k)}, there are infinitely many ℓ ∈ 𝓛^{(k)} with ord(loc_ℓ c_3) ≥ ord(c_3) − e and R loc_ℓ c_1 + R loc_ℓ c_2 containing 𝔪^{d_1+d_2+2e}(R^{(k)} ⊕ R^{(k)}). (Corollary 3.3.7) For c_1, c_2 as above there are infinitely many ℓ ∈ 𝓛^{(k)} with ord(loc_ℓ c_1) ≥ ord(c_1) − e and R loc_ℓ c_1 + R loc_ℓ c_2 ⊇ 𝔪^{k−ord(c_1)+e}R^{(k)} ⊕ 𝔪^{d_1+d_2+2e}R^{(k)}.
items.note: Sah's lemma for a scalar u ∈ U, the α/α^{−1} eigenspace separation under complex conjugation (costing C_α), Nekovář's Cor. (6.3.4) and Lem. (6.6.1) with the quadratic form q on Z⁺, then Čebotarev for Frob_ℓ = τz. The selection of (ψ⁺, ψ⁻) in the proof is invalid as written, though the needed pair exists (sourceIssues).

items.name: Rank one from a non-zero Kolyvagin class
items.statement: Suppose α ≠ 1. If κ_{α,1} ∈ H¹(K, T) is non-zero, then ε = 1, and for k ≫ 0 every element of M^{(k)}(1) has order < k; in particular H¹_F(K, T) ≅ R.
items.note: With s = ind(κ_1) and k > s + 3e, every c_2 ∉ Rc_1 satisfies π^{s+3e}c_2 ∈ Rc_1, by Corollary 3.3.7, the finite–singular relation and global duality between T_α and T_{α^{−1}} (complex conjugation). The opening claim ε ≥ 1 is not justified as stated (sourceIssues).

items.name: Algebra of finite R-modules for the induction
items.statement: (Lemma 3.3.9) If N ⊂ M are finitely generated torsion R-modules with invariants d_1(N) ≥ ⋯ ≥ d_r(N) and d_1(M) ≥ ⋯ ≥ d_s(M), then r ≤ s and d_i(N) ≤ d_i(M). (Lemma 3.3.10, Proposition 3.3.11) Given 0 → X → R/𝔪^k ⊕ M → R/𝔪^{k−a} ⊕ R/𝔪^b → 0 and 0 → X → R/𝔪^k ⊕ M′ → R/𝔪^{a′} ⊕ R/𝔪^{k−b′} → 0 with M, M′ each a direct sum of two isomorphic modules (2s = dim M[π], 2s′ = dim M′[π]), k > exp(M) + 2a and a′ ≤ a (3.13): s − 1 ≤ s′ ≤ s + 1, b ≤ exp(M), exp(X) ≤ exp(M) + a; there is i_0 with ⊕_{i≠i_0} M_i ↪ X; X ↪ M′ ⊕ R/𝔪^{exp(X)}; and d_i(M′) ≥ d_{i+2}(M) for i = 1, …, 2s − 2.
items.note: Pure module theory over a DVR, using self-duality of finite R-modules.

items.name: Bounding Selmer groups of anticyclotomic twists
items.statement: Suppose α ≠ 1 and κ_α ∈ 𝐊𝐒(T_α, F_ord, 𝓛_E) has κ_{α,1} ≠ 0. Then H¹_{F_ord}(K, T_α) has rank one and H¹_{F_ord}(K, A_α) ≅ (Φ/R) ⊕ M_α ⊕ M_α for a finite R-module M_α with length_R(M_α) ≤ length_R(H¹_{F_ord}(K, T_α)/Rκ_{α,1}) + E_α, where E_α ∈ Z_{≥0} depends only on C_α, T_pE and rank_{Z_p}R. When ρ_E|_{G_K} is surjective this is Howard's Theorem 1.6.1 with E_α = 0.
items.note: Proof: ind(κ_1) + (3/2)r(M)e ≥ length_R(M_0) (3.14), by building n_0 = 1, n_1, …, n_s with conditions (a)–(e) through Corollary 3.3.7 and Proposition 3.3.11. The printed constant E_α = r(M)e, the arithmetic of two inequality chains, the index range in (b) and the justification of step (e) need correction (sourceIssues).

items.name: Λ-adic divisibility from a Kolyvagin system (residually reducible case)
items.statement: Let M_E = T_pE ⊗ Λ^∨ and 𝐓 = M_E^∨(1) ≅ T_pE ⊗ Λ with the ordinary structure F_Λ (ordinary at both w | p, strict elsewhere on M_E, relaxed on 𝐓), 𝒳 = H¹_{F_Λ}(K, M_E)^∨, 𝔓_0 = (γ − 1). If κ ∈ 𝐊𝐒(𝐓, F_Λ, 𝓛_E) has κ_1 ≠ 0, then H¹_{F_Λ}(K, 𝐓) has Λ-rank one and there is a finitely generated torsion M with (i) 𝒳 ∼ Λ ⊕ M ⊕ M and (ii) char_Λ(M) | char_Λ(H¹_{F_Λ}(K, 𝐓)/Λκ_1) in Λ[1/p, 1/(γ − 1)] (Theorem 3.4.1). If moreover H¹_F(K, E[p^∞]) has Z_p-corank one, the divisibility holds in Λ[1/p] (Corollary 3.4.2).
items.note: Theorem 3.2.1 at the specialisations 𝔔 = (g + p^m) of height-one primes 𝔓 = (g) ≠ (p), (γ − 1) with the error E_α uniformly bounded as m varies, as in Howard's Thm. 2.2.10; near 𝔓_0 the constant C_α blows up, hence the localisation at γ − 1, removed under the corank-one hypothesis.

items.name: Heegner points on X_0(N) and α-stabilised Λ-adic Heegner classes
items.statement: For m prime to N, K[m] is the ring class field of conductor m, 𝒪_m = Z + mO_K, and the cyclic N-isogeny C/O_K → C/(𝔑 ∩ 𝒪_m)^{−1} gives x_m ∈ X_0(N)(K[m]) and P[m] = π(x_m) ∈ E(K[m]). With α the unit root of x² − a_px + p, P[p^k]_α = P[p^k] − α^{−1}P[p^{k−1}] (k ≥ 1), P[1]_α = u_K^{−1}(1 − α^{−1}σ_p)(1 − α^{−1}σ_p^*)P[1] (p split); the points α^{−k}P[p^k]_α are norm-compatible and κ_∞ = lim_k δ(α^{−d(k)} Norm_{K[p^{d(k)}]/K_k} P[p^{d(k)}]_α) ∈ H¹_{F_Λ}(K, 𝐓).
items.note: HE.1 constructs CM points and Heegner points; HE.8 forms the p-stabilised norm-compatible Heegner classes over the anticyclotomic tower with the initial Euler factor.

items.name: The Heegner Kolyvagin system without Howard's residual hypotheses
items.statement: Assume E(K)[p] = 0 (with (Heeg), (disc)). There is a Kolyvagin system κ^Hg ∈ 𝐊𝐒(𝐓, F_Λ, ℒ_E) with κ_1^Hg ∈ H¹_{F_Λ}(K, 𝐓) non-zero. The classes are the images of κ̃_n = Σ_{s∈S} sD_nQ[n] under δ(n) and restriction, where Q[n] = lim_k Q_k[n] ∈ 𝐇[n] satisfy Q_0[n] = ΦP[n], Φ = (p − a_pσ_p + σ_p²)(p − a_pσ_p^* + σ_p^{*2}) for p split (and (p + 1)² − a_p² for p inert), and Norm Q[nℓ] = a_ℓQ[n].
items.note: Howard's Theorem 2.3.1 assumes p ∤ h_K and G_K ↠ Aut(T); the paper replaces these by E(K)[p] = 0 (restriction from K to K[n] is an isomorphism since K[n] and Q(E[p]) are linearly disjoint and E(K_∞)[p] = 0) and notes that Howard's Lemma 2.3.4 survives p | h_K. Non-vanishing of κ_1^Hg is Cornut–Vatsal.

items.name: Heegner-point divisibility in the residually reducible case
items.statement: Assume E(K)[p] = 0. Then H¹_{F_Λ}(K, 𝐓) has Λ-rank one and there is a finitely generated torsion Λ-module M with (i) 𝒳 ∼ Λ ⊕ M ⊕ M and (ii) char_Λ(M) | char_Λ(H¹_{F_Λ}(K, 𝐓)/Λκ_1^Hg) in Λ[1/p, 1/(γ − 1)]; if H¹_F(K, E[p^∞]) has Z_p-corank one, the divisibility holds in Λ[1/p]. The class κ_1^Hg and κ_∞ generate the same Λ-submodule: pr_K(κ_1^Hg) = u_Kα²(β − 1)²κ_0 (p split) or u_Kα²(β² − 1)κ_0 (p inert), β = pα^{−1}.
items.note: Theorem 3.4.1 and Corollary 3.4.2 applied to κ^Hg. The comparison factors were checked: Φ acts on Norm_{K[1]/K}P[1] as (p − a_p + 1)² = ((α − 1)(β − 1))², and (1 − α^{−1})² = (α − 1)²/α².

items.name: Equivalence of the Heegner-point and BDP main conjectures
items.statement: Assume p = v v̄ splits in K and E(K)[p] = 0. The following are equivalent: (i) H¹_{F_Λ}(K, 𝐓) and 𝒳 = H¹_{F_Λ}(K, M_E)^∨ have Λ-rank one and char_Λ(𝒳_tors) ⊃ char_Λ(H¹_{F_Λ}(K, 𝐓)/Λκ_∞)² in Λ_ac; (ii) H¹_{F_Gr}(K, 𝐓) and 𝔛_E are Λ-torsion and char_Λ(𝔛_E)Λ^ur ⊃ (L_E) in Λ^ur ⊗ Q_p. The same holds for the opposite divisibilities.
items.note: Burungale–Castella–Kim, Theorem 5.2, whose proof applies after inverting p without residual irreducibility. HE.8b plans the irreducible, integral form of this comparison.

items.name: The BDP anticyclotomic main conjecture at Eisenstein primes (Theorem C)
items.statement: Let E/Q, p > 2 an Eisenstein prime for E with E[p]^ss = F_p(φ) ⊕ F_p(ψ) and φ|_{G_p} ≠ 1, ω, and K imaginary quadratic with (Heeg), (spl), (disc) and (Sel): the Z_p-corank of Sel_{p^∞}(E/K) is 1. Then 𝔛_E is Λ-torsion and char_Λ(𝔛_E)Λ^ur = (L_E) as ideals of Λ^ur, i.e. Conjecture A holds.
items.locator: §4.2, Theorem 4.2.2, p. 29; Introduction, Theorem C, p. 3
items.note: Theorem 4.1.2 in Λ[1/p] (using (Sel)), Remark 4.1.3 and Proposition 4.2.1 give char(𝔛_E)Λ^ur ⊃ (L_E) in Λ^ur[1/p]; μ = 0 and equal λ (Theorem 2.2.3) upgrade it to equality. Hypotheses (spl) and φ|_{G_p} ≠ 1, ω force E(K)[p] = 0 (checked), so Theorem 4.1.2 applies.

items.name: Perrin-Riou's Heegner-point main conjecture at Eisenstein primes (Corollary D)
items.statement: Let E/Q, p > 2 an Eisenstein prime, K with (Heeg), (disc), (Sel). If E(K)[p] = 0 then 𝒮 and 𝒳 have Λ_ac-rank one and char(𝒳_tors) ⊃ char(𝒮/ℋ)². If also (spl) and φ|_{G_p} ≠ 1, ω, then char_Λ(H¹_{F_Λ}(K, M_E)^∨_tors) = char_Λ(H¹_{F_Λ}(K, 𝐓)/Λκ_∞)² in Λ_ac, so Conjecture B holds (Corollary 4.2.3). If the Heegner point P_K is non-torsion, or κ_0 ≠ 0, then (Sel) holds by Kolyvagin (Remark 4.2.4).
items.locator: §4.2, Corollary 4.2.3 and Remark 4.2.4, p. 29; Introduction, Corollary D, p. 3
items.note: The first part is Theorem 4.1.2; the equality is Theorem 4.2.2 with Proposition 4.2.1.

items.name: Anticyclotomic control theorem with E(K)[p] = 0
items.statement: Let p = v v̄ split in K and H¹_{F_ac}(K, W) (W = E[p^∞]) be the Selmer group with the conditions of 𝔛_E at v, v̄ and the finite condition H¹(K_v, W)_div at v. Assume E(Q_p)[p] = 0, rank E(K) = 1 and #Ш(E/K)[p^∞] < ∞. Then 𝔛_E is Λ-torsion and, for a generator F_E of char_Λ(𝔛_E), #Z_p/F_E(0) = #Ш(E/K)[p^∞]·(#(Z_p/((1 − a_p + p)/p)·log_{ω_E}P)/[E(K):Z·P]_p)²·∏_{w|N} c_w(E/K)_p for any P ∈ E(K) of infinite order.
items.note: Jetchev–Skinner–Wan Theorem 3.3.1 and (3.5.d), whose proof runs with G_K-irreducibility of E[p] replaced by E(K)[p] = 0 (implied by E(Q_p)[p] = 0 as p splits). BSD.6 imports JSW's control in the irreducible case; this is its Eisenstein extension.

items.name: Complex and p-adic Gross–Zagier formulas for the Heegner point P_K
items.statement: With x_1 = [C/O_K → C/𝔑^{−1}], P_K = Σ_σ π(x_1)^σ ∈ E(K), ω_f = 2πif(τ)dτ and π^*ω_E = c_Eω_f: L(E/K, 1) = 0 and L′(E/K, 1) = u_K^{−2}c_E^{−2}|D_K|^{−1/2}·‖ω_E‖²·ĥ(P_K) (Theorem 5.1.2, Gross–Zagier V.2.1); for p > 2 good and split in K, L_E(0) = c_E^{−2}(1 − a_pp^{−1} + p^{−1})²·log_{ω_E}(P_K)² (Theorem 5.1.3, from BDP Thm. 5.13 with k = 2, r = j = 0).
items.note: GZ.8 proves the Gross–Zagier formula with its X_0(N) specialisation and Manin constants; GZ.9 proves the p-adic logarithm formula at the weight-two point outside the interpolation range.

items.name: Greenberg–Vatsal: p-part of BSD in analytic rank zero at Eisenstein primes
items.statement: Let A/Q have good ordinary reduction at p > 2 and a cyclic p-isogeny whose kernel character is either ramified at p and even, or unramified at p and odd. If L(A, 1) ≠ 0 then ord_p(L(A, 1)/Ω_A) = ord_p(#Ш(A/Q)·Tam(A/Q)/#A(Q)_tors²).
items.note: Kolyvagin (finiteness), Greenberg's Cetraro Theorem 4.1 (the Euler characteristic of the cyclotomic Selmer group), the cyclotomic main conjecture from Kato's divisibility and Greenberg–Vatsal Theorem 1.3, and the Mazur–Swinnerton-Dyer interpolation L_A(0) = (1 − α_p^{−1})²L(A, 1)/Ω_A.

items.name: Inputs for the auxiliary field: non-vanishing twists, Gross–Zagier–Kolyvagin and Cornut–Vatsal
items.statement: (Friedberg–Hoffstein, Thms. B.1–B.2) For a weight-two newform, there are infinitely many imaginary quadratic K satisfying finitely many prescribed splitting conditions (D_K < −4 odd, every ℓ | N and p split) with L(E^K, 1) ≠ 0 when the sign of E^K is +1, or ord_{s=1}L(E^K, s) = 1 when it is −1. (Gross–Zagier–Kolyvagin) If ord_{s=1}L(E/K, s) ≤ 1 or the Heegner point P_K is non-torsion, then rank E(K) = ord and Ш(E/K) is finite. (Cornut–Vatsal) The Λ-adic Heegner class κ_1^Hg is non-zero.
items.locator: §5.2, proof of Theorem 5.2.1, p. 31; §5.3, proof of Theorem 5.3.1, p. 32; §4.1, proof of Theorem 4.1.1, p. 28; Remark 4.2.4, p. 29
items.note: RankZeroOneBSD BSD.2 plans quadratic twists with prescribed local conditions and non-vanishing (the Friedberg–Hoffstein/BFH theorem); BSD.3–BSD.4 and HeegnerPointEulerSystems HE.7 the Gross–Zagier–Kolyvagin theorem; HE.8 and HE.8c Cornut–Vatsal non-vanishing.

items.name: p-parity of Selmer coranks
items.statement: For E/Q and an odd prime p of good reduction, (−1)^{corank_{Z_p} Sel_{p^∞}(E/Q)} is the global root number w(E/Q).
items.note: Monsky, Math. Z. 221 (1996), Theorem 1.5; used to fix the sign of the functional equation from the Selmer corank.

items.name: Bhargava–Klagsbrun–Lemke Oliver–Shnidman: 3-isogeny Selmer ranks in quadratic twist families
items.statement: For E/Q with a rational 3-isogeny, a positive proportion of quadratic twists E^χ (ordered by height, with prescribed local conditions) have 3-Selmer rank 0 and a positive proportion have 3-Selmer rank 1, with explicit proportions governed by the logarithmic Selmer ratio (BKLOS Thms. 2.5–2.6).
items.locator: §5.2, proof of Corollary 5.2.3 and Remark 5.2.4, p. 32
items.note: BKLOS, Duke Math. J. 168 (2019). PAPER-BURUNGALE-TIAN-26 routed BKLOS's 3-Selmer results to ArithmeticStatistics ST.5; the local conditions at 3 matter here (sourceIssues E2).

items.name: A p-converse to Gross–Zagier–Kolyvagin at Eisenstein primes (Theorem E)
items.statement: Let E/Q, p > 2 an Eisenstein prime with E[p]^ss = F_p(φ) ⊕ F_p(ψ) and φ|_{G_p} ≠ 1, ω, and r ∈ {0, 1}. If corank_{Z_p} Sel_{p^∞}(E/Q) = r then ord_{s=1}L(E, s) = r, hence rank E(Q) = r and Ш(E/Q) is finite. (Corollary 5.2.2) The same with dim_{F_p} Sel_p(E/Q) = r, since E(Q)[p] = 0.
items.locator: §5.2, Theorem 5.2.1 and Corollary 5.2.2, pp. 31–32; Introduction, Theorem E, p. 3
items.note: Proof: p-parity (Monsky, Thm. 1.5) fixes the root number; choose K with D_K < −4 odd, (Heeg), (spl) and L(E^K, 1) ≠ 0 (r = 1) or ord L(E^K, s) = 1 (r = 0) by Friedberg–Hoffstein-type twist results; then (Sel) holds, Corollary 4.2.3 makes κ_0 ≠ 0, so P_K is non-torsion and Gross–Zagier gives ord L(E/K, s) = 1.

items.name: Rank-zero and rank-one quadratic twists of curves with a rational 3-isogeny
items.statement: Let E/Q have a rational 3-isogeny. Then a positive proportion of the quadratic twists of E have algebraic and analytic rank 1, and a positive proportion have algebraic and analytic rank 0. For 19a3 : y² + y = x³ + x² + x, at least 41.6% of the twists have rank 1 and at least 25% rank 0.
items.locator: §5.2, Corollary 5.2.3 and Remark 5.2.4, p. 32; Introduction, p. 3
items.note: Bhargava–Klagsbrun–Lemke Oliver–Shnidman Thm. 2.6 (3-Selmer ranks in twist families) with Corollary 5.2.2. The proof needs good reduction at 3 for the twists, which fails for every twist when v_3(j(E)) < 0 (sourceIssues).

items.name: p-part of the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer formula in analytic rank one at Eisenstein primes (Theorem F)
items.statement: Let E/Q, p > 2 good ordinary, with a cyclic p-isogeny of kernel F_p(φ), φ|_{G_p} ≠ 1, ω, and φ either ramified at p and odd, or unramified at p and even. If ord_{s=1}L(E, s) = 1 then ord_p(L′(E, 1)/(Reg(E/Q)·Ω_E)) = ord_p(#Ш(E/Q)·∏_ℓ c_ℓ(E/Q)).
items.locator: §5.3, Theorem 5.3.1 and its proof, (5.4)–(5.7), pp. 32–33; Introduction, Theorem F, p. 4
items.note: Choose K with D_K < −4 odd, (Heeg), (spl), L(E^K, 1) ≠ 0; Theorem 4.2.2 at the trivial character, the control theorem 5.1.1 and Theorem 5.1.3 give ord_p#Ш(E/K) = 2ord_p(c_E^{−1}[E(K):ZP_K]) − Σ_w ord_p c_w(E/K); Gross–Zagier gives L′(E, 1)L(E^K, 1)/(Reg Ω_EΩ_{E^K}) = 2^tc_E^{−2}[E(K):ZP_K]²; Theorem 5.1.4 applies to E^K (whose kernel character φε_K is ramified and even, or unramified and odd, and E^K(Q)[p] = 0). The hypothesis is symmetric in φ ↔ ψ = ωφ^{−1}; checked.
